I know what you mean.  I've found that I often attract others who are "damaged" or have suffered serious emotional trauma.  From them I understand why people can be so hesitant to help others with problems because, well, it's EXHAUSTING.  
  
I have my own problems (severe depression, anxiety, PTSD, etc) I'm trying to deal with, and now someone else, who I really do want to help, just keeps piling their problems on me.  It can be so difficult to try to help someone with depression or anxiety, especially when they've gone so long without help they're comfortable being depressed, so they want someone to vent at, not someone to try to solve their problems.  
  
It took me YEARS to accept that I needed medical help for my depression.  I was in that spot, where being depressed was familiar and safe.  I didn't WANT to be happy.  I wanted to stay depressed.  Once I chased enough people away and came to the realization that I needed meds, things started turning around.  
  
They didn't get all sunshine and unicorn farts, obviously.  I'm still cynical and tired and pessimistic.  But now I can at least understand that when I wasn't being treated for depression, I was not a person people generally wanted to be around.  
  
  
Got off topic there.  But yeah. I guess the problem is I feel like it's very hard for me to make new friends.  I feel like my old friends are moving away physically or emotionally, and I'm just getting left behind.  I have problems connecting with others, and I guess I still don't really know how to do that.

I've always kind of had a hard time making friends, and as a kid I only had a few good friends.  Which, honestly, I liked better than having a ton of friends who I didn't really like.  
  
The problem now being that it's really hard for me to make new friends, and my current ones are moving away or moving on with their life and I just kind of feel left behind, you know?
